data.additional_information:
About the role
SciSpace is building AI products that researchers use daily. We’re hiring PhD scholars/postdocs as part-time Research Fellows to evaluate SciSpace workflows, identify failure modes, and help design benchmarks (in collaboration with us) that measure what matters to researchers.
What you’ll do
1) Research workflow evaluation
Break down real-world researcher workflows for (literature review, method selection, experiment planning, paper writing, peer review response, computational biology, etc.).
Audit SciSpace outputs on these workflows using structured rubrics.
Identify failure modes (e.g., citation mismatch, missing caveats, overconfident claims, wrong assumptions, outdated methods).
2) Build evaluation rubrics and test suites
Define “what good looks like” for a workflow in your domain.
Create scoring rubrics, annotation guidelines, and error taxonomies.
Help set up gold-standard evaluation procedures (adjudication, ambiguity rules, consistency checks).
3) Benchmark design and publishing
Propose benchmark tasks grounded in real workflows.
Create small labeled datasets / gold answers / reference sets.
Collaborate with SciSpace to launch public or internal benchmarks, and write dataset cards / methodology notes.
4) Provide domain research insights
Flag subtle but important issues: methodological rigor, statistical validity, causal vs correlational claims, limitations, reproducibility, appropriate sources.
Recommend product changes that improve researcher trust and outcomes.


What success looks like (deliverables)
Clear workflow maps + “top issues” memos (every 2–4 weeks).
Rubrics + annotation guidelines that another reviewer can apply consistently.
Labeled evaluation sets (e.g., 50–300 items over time, depending on scope).
A benchmark seed that can be shipped internally (and optionally externally) with documentation.
Who should apply
Required
PhD candidate, PhD, or postdoc in a non-ML research field (e.g., biology, medicine, chemistry, physics, materials, EE, mechanical engineering, economics, psychology, etc.).
Demonstrated research maturity: can judge evidence quality, limitations, and methodological correctness.
Strong writing and critical thinking (can write concise memos and rubrics).
Comfort giving direct, constructive feedback and working with product/engineering teams.
Reliability: can ship concrete artifacts on a schedule (not just ideas).
Nice to have
Experience as a reviewer (journal/conference) or mentoring junior researchers.
Familiarity with literature workflows and tools (Zotero/Mendeley, Semantic Scholar, etc.).
Basic comfort with spreadsheets / light scripting for organizing evaluation data.
Interest in open benchmarks / reproducible research artifacts.
